exposure: mode of birth (Cesarean section vs. vaginal birth)
cohort: 71 mother-infant dyads were enrolled and divided into birthing groups, vaginal or Cesarean.
finding: Cesarean section was associated with a weaker newborn intraoral vacuum within 24 hours postpartum, and a stronger intraoral vacuum was related to an earlier onset of maternal lactation.
mod_finding: Newborns born vaginally had significantly stronger peak and baseline intraoral vacuums compared to those born via Cesarean section.
